newsitem.title: UK: UK Estates down after Ashquay bid fails.
newsitem.headline: UK Estates down after Ashquay bid fails.

text.p: Shares in property development firm UK Estates Plc fell on Tuesday after Ashquay said its hostile bid for the company had failed.
By 1335 GMT, UK Estates' shares were down 14 percent, or 4p, at 24-1/2p in light trade of 15,000 shares.
UK Estates said it was delighted the bid had failed, although defending it had been costly.

"The necessity, in the best interests of our shareholders, of defending this unwelcome bid has been a costly exercise and has required considerable time and effort," said executive chairman David Gradel.
"However, it will not deflect us from our ongoing strategy of achieving planned growth, realising profit, growing rental income and achieving opportunities to realise shareholder value," he said.
Ashquay shares were marked down 2-1/2p by 1340 GMT at 37-1/2p although no trade was registered in the stock.
